title: The grapes
subtitle: Native grapes
objectives: Explain the role of international grapes

steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Nero d'Avola is Sicily's most planted red: dark, juicy, with black cherry, plum and fresh acidity. Nerello Mascalese, on Etna, gives pale, perfumed, firm wines; Nerello Cappuccio is its partner. Frappato, in the south-east, gives light, floral reds and blends with Nero d'Avola in Cerasuolo di Vittoria.

steps.title: Whites
steps.body: Catarratto is Sicily's most planted grape, used for everyday whites and Marsala. Grillo, a cross of Catarratto and Muscat of Alexandria, gives fresh, citrus whites and is a Marsala grape. Carricante, on Etna, gives taut, citrus, age-worthy whites. Zibibbo, Muscat of Alexandria, makes sweet Passito di Pantelleria.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Sicily's grapes are native and varied.

steps.body: Look for Grillo from western Sicily. It's a fresh, citrus white that offers great value.

steps.prompt: Which is Sicily's most planted grape?
steps.explanation: Catarratto, a white grape, covers the most area.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Nero d'Avola, Nerello Mascalese and Frappato lead the reds
Catarratto, Grillo and Carricante lead the whites
